prompts.text: Which subscription would you miss most if you had to cancel every recurring service?
Recall realising you were still paying for something you'd stopped using.
Pay monthly for flexibility or annually when a service offers a genuine discount?
You're helping a friend compare two streaming plans with different benefits. What matters besides price?
Recurring charges can become invisible because they don't require a new decision each month.
A free trial isn't truly useful when its cancellation terms are hard to understand.
What's the most important detail to check before accepting an automatic renewal?
Tell me about replacing a paid service with a free option that met your needs.
A service quietly removes a feature while keeping its fee unchanged. What would you ask the company?
Keep one premium service you love or several smaller services you use occasionally?
What's something you've repaired that made you appreciate how it was built?
Describe deciding to maintain an old item instead of replacing it.
Learn to mend simple clothing or fix a basic household appliance safely?
A chair needs a small repair, but a replacement is on sale. What should you consider?
The cost of owning an object can continue long after you've paid for it.
Learning basic maintenance can be more valuable than finding the next discount.
Which everyday item would benefit most from being easier to repair?
Recall borrowing a tool instead of buying one you'd use only once.
A community wants to organise a repair workshop. What items should people learn to maintain first?
Buy a well-kept second-hand item or a basic new alternative for the same price?
What do you find most confusing about comparing the cost of different journeys?
Tell me about choosing a slower route and finding an unexpected benefit.
Use public transport with predictable costs or a faster ride that varies in price?
A friend is planning a daily commute to a new job. Which expenses might they overlook?
The cheapest route on paper doesn't always fit someone's schedule or circumstances.
Time, comfort and reliability belong in a conversation about transport value.
Which travel expense surprises people when they plan their first independent trip?
Recall a day you spent less on travel because you planned several errands together.
Our group is comparing two ways to reach a weekend event. What would make the comparison fair?
Pay a little more for a direct trip or save by making a convenient transfer?
What does a good second-hand shop do to help you trust an item?
Describe a pre-owned purchase that had an interesting story behind it.
Browse used books for hidden discoveries or second-hand furniture for practical pieces?
You find two used bicycles with different wear. What would you inspect before choosing one?
Buying an older item can be rewarding when the seller explains its condition clearly.
A clear return policy can matter more than a persuasive sales description.
Which category of used goods would you always want to inspect in person?
Tell me about passing on an item that someone else found genuinely useful.
A neighbourhood wants to organise a swap event. How might it keep exchanges fair and welcoming?
Exchange rarely used tools with neighbours or organise a seasonal clothing swap?
What makes a small business's pricing feel transparent to you?
Recall learning about the hidden effort behind a handmade product's price.
Buy from a business that explains its costs or one that emphasises speed and convenience?
A home baker wants to price cupcakes fairly. Which ingredients and expenses should be considered?
Customers often see the product but not the preparation, transport or time behind it.
The cheapest seller isn't always the most sustainable choice for a neighbourhood.
Which small local service do you think people regularly undervalue?
Describe an encounter with a business owner who helped you understand their craft.
A new café wants to create a loyalty programme without confusing customers. What should it offer?
Pay for a custom-made item or choose a ready-made version available immediately?
What payment safety habit do you wish more people learnt early?
Describe discovering a suspicious message before it caused a financial problem.
Use spending alerts after every transaction or review your account activity at a regular time?
A message claims you must pay an unexpected fee through a strange link. What would you verify first?
Scammers often create urgency so people skip the checks they normally perform.
A payment method should be judged partly by how it handles mistakes and disputes.
Which detail would make you suspicious of an unfamiliar online shop?
Recall helping somebody recognise that a supposed bargain was too good to be true.
You receive a duplicate payment confirmation. What records would help you resolve it safely?
Make an important purchase through a trusted marketplace or directly from a verified seller?
What's a practical example that helps explain why people buy insurance?
Tell me about learning the difference between a routine expense and an unexpected one.
Understand basic insurance terms or learn how warranties differ from guarantees?
Someone is comparing two phone-protection plans. What exclusions might matter more than the headline fee?
Financial protection products can sound simple until the conditions need explaining.
A clear explanation of what's not covered is as important as a list of benefits.
Which financial term should never be explained using only technical language?
Recall an everyday example that helped you understand the idea of financial risk.
A community workshop introduces the concept of an emergency fund. What relatable example might help?
Compare ways to prepare for small surprises or learn how claims processes work?
What's a surprising way a community has pooled resources for a shared purpose?
Describe watching neighbours work together to make an event affordable.
Contribute supplies to a community project or offer time and a useful skill?
A local group wants to improve its reading room with small contributions. How should it explain the budget?
People are more willing to contribute when they understand how resources will be used.
Transparent record-keeping matters even when a project handles only small amounts.
Which shared facility would make everyday life easier for people in your area?
Recall a fundraiser that made a visible difference in your community.
Volunteers raise more funds than needed for an activity. How might they decide on the remainder?
Support a clearly defined one-off project or a smaller recurring community programme?
Which public service do you notice most when it works reliably?
Tell me about learning how an everyday service is funded or maintained.
Read a simple explanation of local taxes or learn how public project budgets are decided?
A town can improve either street lighting or park maintenance this year. What information should residents receive?
Many public costs are easiest to understand when linked to a service people use.
Good budget explanations should allow ordinary residents to ask meaningful questions.
What local improvement would you want to understand the cost of before debating it?
Recall hearing a practical explanation of a public expense that changed your perspective.
A school committee wants to report how donated funds were spent. What should its summary include?
See an accessible chart of community spending or read short stories about completed projects?
Which everyday technology do you think will most change how people spend money in ten years?
Recall seeing a shopping habit change rapidly after a new service became common.
Explore how contactless payments work or learn what makes online marketplaces trustworthy?
A future shop opens without traditional checkout counters. What customer concerns should it address?
A technology can make payments faster without making purchase decisions any simpler.
Progress in financial tools should be measured by clarity and trust, not just novelty.
What money-related skill will people still need even if most transactions become automated?
Describe a payment method your family once used regularly that now seems old-fashioned.
You help design a money-learning game for teenagers. What real-world decision would become the first challenge?
Learn how digital receipts work or explore why some people still prefer physical cash?
